headline: GOOGLE + SAMSUNG
TAKE ON **META**
cover.hook_pick_reason: The rivalry hook names all three companies and the stakes, and slides 2 to 3 back it with Meta's Omdia market share and Google and Samsung's Dec 10 launch. The $395 hook is backed by slide 4 but leaves out the fight. The 85% claim is backed by slide 2 but names no challenger. The Dec 10 hook is backed by slide 1 but is vaguer. No reader-impact hook: the article gives US starting prices and a launch date, but it does not state a clear effect on ordinary readers beyond a product going on sale, and Korean retail prices are not given.
cover.image_prompt: Cinematic close-up of two sleek pairs of smart glasses with thin dark frames resting on a reflective glass surface, one slightly ahead of the other as if in a race, soft blue and amber rim light, shallow depth of field, a blurred futuristic city at night behind them, subtle lens reflections. No text, no letters, no logos, no people.

slides.title: Gemini glasses open for pre-order
body: Google unveiled **Gemini-based AI glasses** with Samsung, Gentle Monster (a Korean eyewear brand) and Warby Parker (a US eyewear brand). Pre-orders opened Nov 12 in Korea and the US. Official launch: **Dec 10**.

slides.title: Meta holds the market
body: Per Omdia, a market research firm, Meta had **85.2%** of global AI glasses shipments last year and 81.3% in the first half of this year. Omdia expects over **15 million** units shipped this year.

slides.title: No display, just Gemini
body: The glasses have **no AR display**. You use voice and visual recognition. They work with Galaxy phones and iPhones, and have a 12MP ultra-wide camera, about 41 g weight and up to **9 hours** of battery.

slides.title: From $395 in the US
body: US starting prices: Warby Parker **$395** (about 530,000 won) and Gentle Monster **$449** (about 600,000 won). The Gentle Monster line sells in Korea and the US. Warby Parker's is US only.

slides.title: Built-in privacy limits
body: Gemini **blurs bystanders' faces** before processing video. Recording stops if the indicator light is covered or tampered with. A physical switch turns the power fully off.

facts.text: Google unveiled a Gemini-based 'Intelligent Eyewear' line made with Samsung, Gentle Monster and Warby Parker; pre-orders began Nov 12 (US time) in Korea and the US.
Official launch date is Dec 10; the Gentle Monster collection sells in Korea and the US, the Warby Parker collection only in the US.
The glasses have no AR display; they work through voice commands and visual recognition, and are compatible with Galaxy phones and iPhones.
They have a 12-megapixel ultra-wide camera and open speakers, weigh about 41 g, and last up to 9 hours on battery.
US starting prices: Gentle Monster $449 (about 600,000 won), Warby Parker $395 (about 530,000 won).
Gemini automatically blurs bystanders' faces before processing video, and recording stops if the indicator light is covered or tampered with; a physical switch turns power fully off.
Omdia says Meta had 85.2% of global AI smart glasses shipments last year and 81.3% in the first half of this year; Omdia expects over 15 million AI glasses shipped this year.

caption:
Google and Samsung just opened pre-orders for Gemini AI glasses, taking on Meta from Dec 10.

Meta holds most of the AI glasses market, per Omdia, a market research firm, and Google and Samsung are now entering it.

→ Pre-orders opened Nov 12 in Korea and the US, with launch on Dec 10
→ US starting prices: $395 (Warby Parker) and $449 (Gentle Monster)
→ Gemini blurs bystanders' faces, and recording stops if the indicator light is covered

Would you wear AI glasses with a camera?

Source: AI Times (in Korean), "Google and Samsung enter the AI glasses market... head-to-head with Meta from Dec 10", Nov 12, 2026.
